After you separate, what stays shared? You open the family album and pause. Who can still see the photos? Dr. Lior Tabansky works through questions like that with you, in person. Before you get in touch The things you set up together Some connections still help you get through the day. Toza checks what each one allows so you can decide what you want to keep. A family cloud account that still shares photos or documents.A recovery number or email that still belongs to your spouse.An old phone or tablet still signed in to your messages.A location-sharing setting you turned on years ago. Know what a change will affect You might want to stop sharing your location and still be able to open the family album. Before you change a password or leave a family plan, it helps to know what else depends on it. Dr. Tabansky checks your own devices, accounts and recovery settings with you. You stay present, enter your own credentials and choose which changes to approve. You agree the sequence together before anything changes. Your attorney can be involved. With your authorization, you receive an attorney-friendly summary of the work and what remains, and timing can be coordinated with counsel. About Dr. Lior Tabansky What happens first? The free private conversation usually takes 10–20 minutes. Dr. Tabansky replies personally. You discuss what prompted you to get in touch, whether anything needs prompt attention and whether an in-person assessment would help. How Toza works Private Exposure Assessment The assessment costs ₪4,000 and takes about half a day in person. You keep a written exposure summary showing what was checked, what remains and which steps come next. If you choose protection work, you agree on its scope and price separately. The assessment fee is credited in full when protection work begins within 30 days of assessment completion.
